method: Fabs and other sites in Germany (one shelved project), the United States, Taiwan and Malaysia, Japan's law for state investment in Rapidus and Saudi Arabia's National Semiconductor Hub, and equipment models for makers with no models (MPI, SCIL, ATLANT 3D, Semilab), from government releases, company releases, product pages and industry news located by web search; titles and search-result summaries.

pr.tech: Automated 300 mm probe system; chucks from ambient to hot up to 300 °C; family variants TS3000-HP, TS3000-SE (shielded environment for low-noise measurement, down to -60 °C) and TS3000-DS (double-sided, for silicon photonics and electro-optical devices) (per MPI data sheet and distributor pages)
pr.app: Product engineering, failure analysis, design validation, wafer-level reliability, silicon photonics, RF and mmW
pr.note: Batch 19: from distributor product and news pages reproducing MPI specifications; check MPI data sheets before relying on figures, as specifications vary by configuration.

pr.tech: Automated 200 mm probe system that can be converted to fully automatic at purchase or later in the field; hot chucks up to 300 °C (per MPI data sheet)
pr.note: Batch 19: from the MPI data sheet as hosted by a distributor.

pr.tech: Fully automatic 300 mm wafer probe system with MPI's WaferWallet material handling; feature set equivalent to the TS3000 and TS3000-SE (per MPI release)
pr.note: Batch 19: from MPI's launch release; release date not captured.

pr.tech: Automated nanoimprint tool using PDMS-based soft stamps and an inorganic sol-gel imprint resist; more than 700 imprints from one stamp reported (SPIE 2018)
pr.app: Volume nanoimprint for photonic and optical devices (e.g., VCSELs, x-ray optics)
pr.note: Batch 19: from a 2018 SPIE paper on AutoSCIL 200 production tooling and the company profile. Company claims of sub-10 nm features on up to 300 mm wafers refer to the SCIL technology, not specifically this model.

pr.tech: Programmable atomic-scale fabrication platform: a localised microreactor deposits materials selectively without masks; SEMI-compliant; more than 450 material families supported (per ATLANT 3D)
pr.app: Materials and device prototyping for RF and microelectronics, advanced packaging, photonics, MEMS and sensors, and quantum technologies
pr.note: Batch 19: filed under ALD as the closest taxonomy entry; DALP is a selective, maskless atomic-layer process. Capability figures are company claims.

pr.tech: Photo-modulated reflectivity measurement for in-line implant monitoring on product wafers; the PMR signal responds to implant damage and carrier concentration; PMR-3000S dose-monitor variant (per Semilab)
pr.app: Ion implant dose and process monitoring
pr.note: Batch 19: from Semilab's product page and a product listing; throughput and wafer sizes not captured.

pr.tech: Tabletop platform for semiconductor material characterisation, including heavy- and transition-metal contamination and crystal defects; wafers up to 300 mm (per Semilab)
pr.app: Material and contamination characterisation in mid-range fabs and laboratories
pr.note: Batch 19: from Semilab product pages; a WT-2000 PL variant is also listed.

pr.tech: Stand-alone wafer testers for high-volume 300 mm fabs, with full factory automation and overhead-transport (OHT) loading (per Semilab)
pr.app: In-fab contamination and material monitoring in high-volume 300 mm fabs
pr.note: Batch 19: three models listed together on one Semilab product page; differences between them not captured.

fa.name: Wolfspeed SiC fab, Ensdorf (Saarland), shelved
fa.scheme: Federal and Saarland state subsidies promised (amount not captured in reviewed sources)

invest.label: Around €2.7 billion planned, including ZF's €170 million; some reports say about €2 billion (per coverage)

fa.products: SiC power devices for electric vehicles
fa.notes: Planned on the site of a former coal-fired power station on the Saar. In Oct 2024 reports said ZF was pulling out and Wolfspeed had postponed the project indefinitely, citing weak EV demand; ZF said the delays lay with Wolfspeed. Wolfspeed said the plant was not scrapped entirely, so it is recorded as paused, not cancelled. Nothing after late 2024 was found in reviewed sources. The 200 mm wafer size is from the original plan.

fa.name: Bosch silicon carbide fab, Roseville (California)
fa.scheme: CHIPS and Science Act direct funding of up to $225 million (preliminary terms Dec 2024; agreement finalised Jul 2026)
fa.technology: Silicon carbide power semiconductors; front-end manufacturing plus back-end test, sort and dicing
fa.notes: Bosch bought an existing wafer fab in 2023 and is converting it to silicon carbide, replacing most of the equipment but keeping the cleanrooms and workforce. Sample production has begun; commercial output on 200 mm wafers is planned for 2026 but was not confirmed in reviewed sources. The CHIPS award is milestone-based.

fa.name: PSMC Tongluo 12-inch fab, Miaoli

invest.label: NT$300 billion (total project, per Focus Taiwan)
NT$80 billion spent by the May 2024 opening (per coverage)

fa.capacity: Designed for 50,000 12-inch wafers a month (per Focus Taiwan)
fa.technology: 55, 40 and 28 nm (trial production at opening); silicon interposers for CoWoS-type packaging (per TrendForce)
fa.notes: Ownership is unresolved. Taiwan News reports describe Micron completing a NT$57.7 billion purchase of the fab and PSMC moving staff, tools and product lines back to Hsinchu, while a Dec 2025 TrendForce report says Micron was still weighing a purchase. The operator is left as PSMC until a primary source confirms a sale. The two investment figures cover different scopes (total plan vs spent at opening).

fa.name: AT&S IC substrate plant, Kulim Hi-Tech Park (Kedah)

invest.label: About RM5 billion invested in the plant and administrative building to date (per AT&S, May 2025)

fa.products: IC substrates, almost exclusively for AMD (per MIDA)
fa.jobs: About 1,500 (May 2025, per AT&S); 2,500 planned for phase 1 (per MIDA)
fa.notes: AT&S's first plant in Southeast Asia, opened 24 Jan 2024 with production due to start later; high-volume manufacturing announced 5 May 2025. A second phase was under construction at the opening. The two investment figures likely differ in scope (project value vs spent to date).

fa.name: Lam Research manufacturing plant, Batu Kawan (Penang)
fa.notes: Described as Lam's largest manufacturing facility and the hub for its Asia manufacturing operations. Opening slipped from a planned May 2021 to 3 Aug 2021; the plant grew from a planned 700,000 sq ft. An automated warehouse with Malaysia's largest automated storage and retrieval system was added in 2024 (per InvestPenang).

pg.name: Japan amended Information Processing Promotion Act (state investment in Rapidus through the IPA)

facts.label: Cabinet approval
facts.value: 7 Feb 2025: amendments to the Information Processing Promotion Act and the Special Accounts Act

facts.label: Mechanism
facts.value: Lets the Information-technology Promotion Agency (IPA), overseen by METI, invest directly in chip companies and guarantee private loans; Rapidus is the intended recipient

facts.label: Passage
facts.value: Passed in the 2025 ordinary Diet session (per TrendForce); the exact date was not confirmed in reviewed sources

facts.label: Investments
facts.value: ¥100 billion of government equity in Rapidus through the IPA (per Jiji); further investment reported in June 2026

facts.label: Reported scale
facts.value: About US$16 billion of state backing for Rapidus (Bloomberg headline, Apr 2026); further ¥1 trillion of support reportedly planned (TrendForce, Nov 2025)

pg.match: Information Processing Promotion Act|Information-technology Promotion Agency

facts.label: Launched
facts.value: 5 Jun 2024 at the Future of the Semiconductor Forum in Riyadh

facts.label: Funding
facts.value: SAR 1 billion (about US$266 million) fund to attract fabless chip design firms, plus access to SAR 150 million of support from the National Technology Development Program

facts.label: Targets by 2030
facts.value: At least 50 chip design companies; 5,000 engineers trained in semiconductor design; 25 senior experts attracted through premium residency

facts.label: Progress
facts.value: Feb 2025: the hub's head, Naveed Sherwani, said 10 companies, mostly from Silicon Valley, would start operating in Riyadh within two to three months
